body:
elaine: quick thread — were seeing lots of idle-but-open streaming connections that hog gateway slots. typical pattern: sdk opens stream, sends a token, then next token 20s later. capacity accounting treats them as active and it spikes quotas. should we split connection admission from GPU compute admission?

sam: yes. this shows up in our load tests too. it skews slot counts and OOM risk on kvcache.

miguel: twofold problem: admission accounting and memory TTLs for kvcache entries. currently both tied to an 'active slot' boolean.

anya: proposal: introduce light-weight "conn slot" vs heavy "compute slot". conn slot holds minimal metadata and network file descriptors but not batch capacity. compute slot required when request joins a batch or sends rapid tokens.

ryan: how does transition happen if a conn suddenly bursts? we need sub-second promotion to compute or app UX will suffer.

anya: plan: credit pool per-tenant. each conn gets credits (e.g., 5) that permit out-of-band token emissions without promotion. credits drip at configurable rate. when exhausted, tokens are backpressured until promoted. promotions are attempted immediately and honored within compute_prep_timeout.

miguel: re: implementation: admission state machine needs to track credit_balance, last_emit_ts, conn_state. also influence kvcache TTL: conn-only streams get aggressive eviction when credit_balance==0.

sam: pseudo-config example: 

```
admission:
  max_compute_slots: 2048
  max_conn_slots: 8192
  tenant_credit_rate: 2/min
  tenant_burst_credits: 6
  compute_prep_timeout_ms: 500
```

anya: compute_prep_timeout default 500ms but tenant-overridable up to a safe cap (2s). SDKs can hint expected burstiness via header X-Client-Burst: <n> to pre-warm credits.

elaine: we should provide explicit feedback to clients. streaming-only case: initial 202 + X-Conn-Credits: 6. when we start backpressuring send a trailer with X-Admit-Status: throttled and Retry-After. For non-streaming (HTTP request) send 429.

ryan: observability: need metrics per-tenant: conn_slots, compute_slots, credit_balance, promotions, promotion_latency histo. traces must annotate why a promotion rejected.

miguel: billing implications: either a tiny per-minute conn fee or roll into memory footprint billing. otherwise potential for DOS via lots of idle conns. suggest per-conn-minute meter for conn-only.

sam: scheduling: preemption and fairness. if many promotions arrive simultaneously, scheduler must avoid head-of-line blocking. Prefer a small promote-queue that feeds the micro-batcher with priority windows.

anya: security/network consideration: some proxies or middleboxes may tear idle TCP flows. need fallback: SDKs should re-open stream on RST and honor backoff to avoid amplifying load. add guidance to Private docs.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started: gateway/edge-credit-admit v0.3 -> edge-canary

elaine: next steps: miguel assignee for RFC (state machine + kvcache TTLs) due EOW; sam to add scenario tests to gabby-sim; anya to spec metrics + header formats. please post any abuse patterns or dataset queries here.

ryan: linking incident notes: https://redwood.internal/ops/incidents/2026-03-stream-abuse (internal)

sam: +1

elaine: awesome, closing thread once RFC is up.
